summary: Exhaustive end-user reality audit of every VenueOS surface (live API + DB + code path) + signup black-box across 3 browsers, synthesized into a ranked bug list
logs: Wave 1: auditing 16 surfaces + signup black-box on 3 browsers

audits.summary:
The signup funnel works end-to-end and a real new user DOES get a usable, auto-logged-in workspace. Live-verified: POST /api/v1/signup (NOT /onboarding/signup as the brief stated — that path 403s as a non-route) validates input, creates tenant+user+audit_log in a transaction (onboarding.service.ts:135-178), seeds vertical sample data, auto-logs in, and redirects to /onboarding/branding → dashboard. Proof in DB: a "Beta Test" K12 tenant signed up 2026-06-26 with 1 ACTIVE user + 1 audit row. The signup page (apps/web/src/app/signup/page.tsx) is polished, 12-vertical-aware, professional. The dashboard has a real 3-step getting-started guide so new tenants aren't stranded on a blank slate.

BUT the most serious issue is a security costume: the @Throttle({default:{limit:5}}) on the public account-creation endpoint is NOT enforcing — I fired 8 rapid valid-shape requests and got zero 429s (all 409s). The global ThrottlerModule default of 600/min is effectively the only limit, so the documented 5/min anti-abuse protection on signup (and the same pattern on password-reset 3/hr, invite-accept 5/min) is theater. Combined with no email-verification gate, anyone can mass-create tenants/users. Secondary: the "auto-seed populated dashboard" comment over-promises for K12/most verticals — it seeds streaming/ads connections but ZERO templates/playlists/assets/screens (DB-confirmed for the beta tenant). Also surfaced weak prod JWT/SESSION secrets and a leaked GitHub PAT in Railway env (flagged as a spawned task).

Local tree note: code paths matched live behavior; findings are not stale.

findings.title: Per-route @Throttle on public signup is a costume — rate limit never fires (5/min not enforced; 600/min global is the real cap)
findings.userRepro: curl -X POST https://api-production-39a1.up.railway.app/api/v1/signup -d '{"districtName":"Acme Coffee — Hartford","slug":"acme-hartford","adminEmail":"x@example.invalid","password":"abcd1234efgh","vertical":"K12"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' — fire it 8 times in a row.
findings.evidence: LIVE: 8 consecutive valid-shape requests all returned 409 (reached business logic), ZERO returned 429. The decorator declares 5/min but @nestjs/throttler's named-throttler 'default' override does not bind to the UNNAMED forRoot config (app.module.ts:158 has no name key), so only the global 600/min applies. 600/min on an unauthenticated, account-creating endpoint = effectively unlimited abuse. Same broken pattern affects password-reset (3/hr) and invite-accept (5/min) — all the auth-abuse guards are non-functional.

findings.title: Production signs every signup auto-login JWT with a guessable secret (JWT_SECRET / SESSION_SECRET = 'super_secure_beta_..._xYz')
findings.file: Railway api service env (project graceful-embrace, id 5220b230-9824-4c95-862e-74bb657b2312); consumed by apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts:178 (jwtService.sign at signup)
findings.userRepro: Sign up at https://venue-os.app/signup → you are auto-logged-in with a JWT signed by JWT_SECRET. An attacker who guesses the trivially-patterned secret can forge a session token for ANY tenant/user, including SUPER_ADMIN.
findings.evidence: Railway list_variables: JWT_SECRET=super_secure_beta_jwt_secret_2026_xYz and SESSION_SECRET=super_secure_beta_session_secret_2026_xYz — both human-guessable, in NODE_ENV=production. CLAUDE.md mandates 64-char hex random secrets; these violate it and are the load-bearing secret for the signup→auto-login token. (Spawned a rotation task; this is a known launch blocker from the 2026-06-08 audit still live.)

findings.title: 'Auto-seed a populated dashboard' over-promises: new K12/most-vertical tenants get 0 templates, 0 playlists, 0 assets, 0 screens
findings.file: apps/api/src/onboarding/onboarding.service.ts:182-187 (comment claims 'populated dashboard rather than a blank slate'); apps/api/src/sample-data/sample-data.service.ts:58-98 (seedForNewTenant only seeds POS/streaming/ads connections)
findings.userRepro: Sign up as a K-12 school → land on dashboard. The KPI cards read 'No screens paired yet', Library 0, Playing Now 0. The only seeded artifact (9 public-broadcaster stream channels) is invisible because nothing places it on a screen.
findings.evidence: DB for the live beta-test K12 tenant: templates=0, playlists=0, assets=0, screens=0, screen_groups=0, users=1. seedForNewTenant seeds only stream_provider_connections(1)+stream_channels(9)+ad_network_connections(1) for K12; restaurant menus only for QSR/RESTAURANT/BAR, retail SKUs only for RETAIL/FASHION. Mitigated by the dashboard's real 3-step getting-started guide (dashboard/page.tsx:561-564) and 373 shared system templates being browseable — so it's P1 (misleading claim + weaker first-run), not a broken flow.

findings.title: No email-verification gate: any syntactically-valid email instantly mints a live, auto-logged-in workspace
findings.file: apps/api/src/onboarding/onboarding.service.ts:64-189 (no verification step); user created with status:'ACTIVE' at line 154
findings.userRepro: Sign up with any fake-but-valid-format email (e.g. nobody@nowhere.invalid) → you immediately get a working ACTIVE tenant + admin session; the address is never confirmed.
findings.evidence: Live beta tenant user beta+1782407641605@venue-os.app is status=ACTIVE with no verification. validateEmail (onboarding.service.ts:39-41) only regex-checks shape. Acceptable for a pilot per the brief ('no email gate'), but with the P0 broken throttle this is an unbounded junk-tenant / spam-relay vector (welcome mail fires to the unverified address). Flagging so it's a conscious decision, not an oversight.

findings.title: Generic validation error gives the operator no field-level reason on signup failure
findings.file: apps/web/src/app/signup/page.tsx:236-245 (shows data.message); apps/api error envelope returns {code:'ValidationError', message:'Bad Request Exception'}
findings.userRepro: If client-side checks are bypassed (e.g. a too-long org name >200 chars), the server returns 'Bad Request Exception' with no indication of WHICH field is wrong; the signup form surfaces that raw string.
findings.evidence: LIVE: POST /api/v1/signup with {} returns {"error":true,"code":"ValidationError","message":"Bad Request Exception"} — no field path. The Zod pipe's per-field detail is dropped before reaching the client. Low impact because the form does client-side validation first (page.tsx:214-216), so most users never see it; still a UX gap if any server-only rule fails.

findings.title: Stale tenant exists with vertical 'FITNESS' that is not in the canonical VERTICALS list (data hygiene)
findings.file: packages/api-types/src/verticals.ts:40-68 (canonical list has GYM, not FITNESS)
findings.userRepro: Not user-reproducible via current signup (the gate correctly rejects bogus verticals — verified live: vertical 'NOTAREALVERTICAL' → 400 'Invalid vertical.'). It's a legacy row.
findings.evidence: DB: tenant 'Gym Demo' (slug gym-demo, created 2026-04-21) has vertical='FITNESS', which isVertical() now rejects. Pre-dates the canonical list. Any code that maps vertical→templates/copy will mis-handle this one tenant (falls through to K12 defaults). Minor; just clean the row to GYM.

costumes: @Throttle({limit:5}) on POST /api/v1/signup — declared but never enforces (live: 8 rapid requests, 0x 429); same for password-reset 3/hr and invite-accept 5/min
onboarding.service.ts:182 comment 'land on a populated dashboard rather than a blank slate' — for K12/most verticals the dashboard is empty (0 templates/playlists/assets/screens)

audits.surface: auth-roles-session (login, JWT/session, RBAC role guards, canTriggerPanic, JWT revocation, cross-domain web↔api auth)
audits.summary: Core auth WORKS end-to-end and the architecture is genuinely solid: login returns a verified JWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET, 1h / 30d-rememberMe), the FE stores it in sessionStorage/localStorage and sends it as a Bearer header (so cross-domain venue-os.app↔railway.app auth needs no third-party cookie — a clean design), Zod-bounds the login body, argon2id with a timing-equalizing dummy-verify on the miss branch (no email enumeration), and tenant isolation is enforced the RIGHT way: every controller scopes off the verified `req.user.tenantId` from the JWT, NOT the cosmetic `[schoolId]` URL segment. I verified live: bad creds → 401, empty/malformed body → ValidationError, no/garbage token → 401, and the DB shows the AuditLog forensic trail is real (671 AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCESS, AUTH_LOGIN_FAILED rows including my own probe). Role-escalation is gated (assertCallerCanAssignRole), and the per-user mass-revocation safeguard (role-downgrade / canTriggerPanic→false → markUserTokensInvalid → guard reads getTokenInvalidBefore) is fully wired on BOTH read and write sides — NOT a costume. The RbacGuard's RESTRICTED_VIEWER read-only logic and SUPER_ADMIN override are correct. BUT three real defects: (1) the login brute-force rate limit is a COSTUME in production — the ThrottlerModule uses default in-memory storage with no Redis backing, so across the multiple Railway replicas each has its own counter; 14 rapid same-IP bad logins all returned 401 (never 429) and x-ratelimit-remaining bounced non-monotonically (8,6,7,5,4,6,5,4,3,2,8,6,4,7) — direct proof of independent counters. The MFA limiter's own code comment FALSELY claims the per-IP layer is "Redis-backed in prod via the existing ThrottlerModule." (2) Logout is client-side-only — the "Log out" button calls only the Zustand store clear + redirect; NO web code path ever calls POST /auth/logout, so the server-side JWT revocation (the whole jwt_revoked_list machinery) never fires from the UI; DB confirms 0 AUTH_LOGOUT rows against 671 logins. An exfiltrated token stays valid up to 30 days even after the operator "logs out." (3) The JWT lives in localStorage/sessionStorage (not HttpOnly), so it's XSS-readable — acceptable given the cross-domain Bearer design, but it makes #2 worse since the only kill-switch (server revocation) is unreachable from the button. SSO (SAML/OIDC) and MFA are fully built but UNUSED in prod (0 SSO configs, 0 MFA-enrolled users across 16 users) — unverified in the wild, not costumes per se. Local-tree note: findings traced against the working tree; live commit is 79720947, so #1/#2 could in principle differ from prod, but the LIVE header-bounce and LIVE 0-logout-rows confirm both in production.
costumes: Login brute-force rate limit: @Throttle({ttl:60000,limit:10}) on auth.controller.ts:36 is backed by ThrottlerModule.forRoot in-memory storage (app.module.ts:158, no Redis storage option anywhere in apps/api/src) — across multiple Railway replicas it never trips; 14 same-IP bad logins all 401, x-ratelimit-remaining bounced 8→6→7→5→4→6...→7 instead of decrementing to 0/429

Server-side logout / JWT revocation: POST /api/v1/auth/logout (auth.controller.ts:156, SADDs token to jwt_revoked_list) is fully built but has ZERO web callers — store.logout() (ui-store.ts:210) only clears storage + redirects; DB shows 0 AUTH_LOGOUT rows vs 671 logins

MFA-rate-limiter code comment (mfa-rate-limiter.ts:10-12) asserts the per-IP layer is 'Redis-backed in prod via the existing ThrottlerModule config' — false; ThrottlerModule has no Redis storage, making the documented defense-in-depth claim untrue

findings.title: Login brute-force rate limit is ineffective in production (in-memory throttler across multiple Railway replicas)
findings.userRepro: From one IP, POST /api/v1/auth/login 14× rapidly with the same bad credentials. Expected: 429 after 10/min. Actual: all 14 returned 401, none 429. Live evidence: x-ratelimit-remaining bounced non-monotonically (8,6,7,5,4,6,5,4,3,2,8,6,4,7) instead of counting down to 0 — proof that requests hit independent per-replica in-memory counters.
findings.evidence: ThrottlerModule.forRoot([{ttl:60000,limit:600}]) with NO storage option = default in-memory ThrottlerStorageService. grep for ThrottlerStorageRedis/storage:/nestjs-throttler-storage in apps/api/src returns nothing. Railway project 'graceful-embrace' runs the api service load-balanced; the bouncing live header confirms >1 counter. The per-IP 10/min login limit and global 600/min limit are both multiplied by replica count and reset on LB re-route. argon2's ~45ms cost is the only remaining brake. Fix: back ThrottlerModule with @nest-lab/throttler-storage-redis (Redis already provisioned as a Railway service).

findings.title: "Log out" never revokes the JWT server-side — token stays valid up to 30 days after logout
findings.userRepro: Log in (especially with 'Keep me logged in' → 30d token). Click Log out. The UI clears and redirects to /login. But the JWT issued at login is never added to jwt_revoked_list, so anyone holding a copy of that token (XSS exfil, shared/stolen device that synced localStorage, copied Bearer) can keep calling the API until natural expiry (1h, or 30d for rememberMe).
findings.evidence: store.logout() only does sessionStorage/localStorage.removeItem + set({token:null}) + notifyExplicitLogout(); it does NOT call apiFetch('/auth/logout'). grep across apps/web/src finds no caller of '/auth/logout'. DB confirms the endpoint is never exercised: SELECT count(*) FROM audit_logs WHERE action='AUTH_LOGOUT' = 0, against 671 AUTH_LOGIN_SUCCESS rows. The server revocation machinery (jwt_revoked_list SADD + 503-when-Redis-down) is correct but dead from the UI. Fix: have logout() await POST /auth/logout (best-effort, before clearing local state).

findings.title: JWT stored in localStorage/sessionStorage (non-HttpOnly) — XSS-readable, and its only kill-switch is unreachable
findings.file: apps/web/src/store/ui-store.ts:27-86 (bootstrapAuth) & 181-208 (login persists to localStorage on rememberMe) + apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (Authorization: Bearer from useUIStore token)
findings.userRepro: Open dev console on the dashboard after login and read window.localStorage['edu_cms_token'] (or sessionStorage). Any injected script on venue-os.app can do the same and exfiltrate a 30-day bearer.
findings.evidence: Token is deliberately in web storage to make cross-domain auth (venue-os.app → api.railway.app) work via Bearer header without a third-party cookie — a reasonable trade. But it is not HttpOnly, so it is XSS-exposed, and because logout doesn't revoke server-side (finding above), an exfiltrated token cannot be killed. The two findings compound. Mitigation options: ship server-side logout (fixes the kill-switch), add a short refresh-token rotation path, and/or move to an HttpOnly cookie + same-site=None for same-site deploys. Lower severity because it requires an XSS foothold first.

findings.title: RbacGuard spatial-scope check for DISTRICT_ADMIN is dead code (districtId never in the JWT) — relies entirely on per-controller tenantId scoping
findings.userRepro: Not directly exploitable today, but a latent trap: any future controller that trusts RbacGuard's district scope check (instead of re-scoping by req.user.tenantId) would be unprotected.
findings.evidence: The login JWT payload is {sub,email,tenantId,role,canTriggerPanic} — it carries NO districtId and NO schoolId. JwtAuthGuard sets districtId: payload.districtId (always undefined) and schoolId: payload.schoolId || payload.tenantId. RbacGuard:121 then compares targetDistrictId !== typedUser.districtId, where typedUser.districtId is undefined, so the DISTRICT_ADMIN branch is effectively inert; the SCHOOL_ADMIN branch only works because schoolId falls back to tenantId. Cross-tenant isolation actually holds because every controller (verified in templates.controller.ts:56, tenants.controller.ts) scopes off req.user.tenantId from the verified JWT and ignores the [schoolId] URL param — so this is a misleading/defense-theater layer, not a live hole. Fix: either drop the dead scope branch or put districtId/schoolId in the JWT and make the check real.

findings.title: SSO (SAML/OIDC) and MFA are fully built but unverified in production (0 configs, 0 enrollments)
findings.userRepro: As an admin, Settings has SSO config + MFA enrollment surfaces, but no tenant has ever completed either flow.
findings.evidence: DB: SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_sso_configs = 0 (0 enabled); SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE mfa_totp_verified_at IS NOT NULL = 0 across 16 users / 671 logins. The code is real (OIDC callback verifies state+nonce from express-session — sso.controller.ts:112-119; SSO redirect returns token via URL #fragment not query, avoiding log/referer leak — sso.controller.ts:254-265; SAML enable is gated to SUPER_ADMIN per the passport-saml CVE interim control). Not a costume, but a production-unexercised path — login.mfaRequired/challenge and the full SSO handshake have never run against a real IdP here, so treat as 'works in theory, unproven live.' Recommend an end-to-end smoke (one test OIDC config + one MFA enrollment) before selling either to a customer.

audits.summary: The dashboard-fleet surface is genuinely real, not a costume. Every KPI is derived from live data, not hardcoded: the per-tenant cards (Fleet Health %, Down, Playing Now, Library, Sites) are computed client-side in apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/dashboard/page.tsx (fleet useMemo L124-139, sites L159-188, liveNowCount L220-226) from useScreens/usePlaylists/useAssets/useSchedules. The HQ multi-location roll-up (FleetRollup.tsx) consumes a real GET /screens/fleet endpoint (screens.controller.ts:1063) that aggregates the parent tenant + its DIRECT children, recomputes each screen's ONLINE/OFFLINE live from last_ping_at (35s window, mirroring the list() mapper), and rolls up State→Location. Verified in DB: Acme Coffee Corporate (DISTRICT_ADMIN) has 50 child locations / 150 screens with addresses+coords, and the State parse produces real states (CA:5, TX:5, FL:4...). The "ONLINE forever" status bug is genuinely fixed — only the 4 Dodgers screens pinging within 35s show ONLINE-live; everything stale correctly flips OFFLINE-live. The tenant switcher routes through an authorized, audited POST /tenants/switch (re-issues JWT, scoped to caller's tree for DISTRICT_ADMIN). Recent Activity is real tenant-scoped audit_logs (/audit/recent). The Phase-2b "HQ notified on child outage" claim is backed by a real scheduled offline-screen-scanner cron, not a costume. Auth gating is solid (all endpoints 401 unauthed with clean error envelopes). Findings are data/role edge-cases, not broken features: the biggest is a role-coverage gap (a SCHOOL_ADMIN who owns a multi-location parent gets no fleet roll-up at all), plus a demo-data freshness issue (all 150 Acme child screens have NULL last_ping_at, so the flagship multi-location demo currently renders as 0/150 online — a sea of red that makes a working feature look broken).

findings.title: SCHOOL_ADMIN of a multi-location parent tenant gets NO fleet roll-up or child-location switcher on the dashboard
findings.userRepro: Log in as gschiemann@e-arc.com (SCHOOL_ADMIN of Chardon High School, which has 2 child schools: Chardon Middle + Fremont Elementary). The dashboard shows only Chardon HS's own 1 screen — no 'Corporate fleet overview', no State→Location tree, no way to see or switch into the 2 child schools. A DISTRICT_ADMIN on the SAME tenant (gschiemann@sbcglobal.net) DOES get the full roll-up.
findings.evidence: Frontend gate: `const canFleet = fleetRole === 'SUPER_ADMIN' || fleetRole === 'DISTRICT_ADMIN'` (dashboard/page.tsx:52) → useFleet({enabled:canFleet}) never fires for SCHOOL_ADMIN. Backend matches: @Get('fleet') @RequireRoles(SUPER_ADMIN, DISTRICT_ADMIN) (screens.controller.ts:1064) — a SCHOOL_ADMIN would 403 even if the FE called it. DB proof: Chardon HS (id 2bf88a7b...) has parent_id=NULL, 2 children with parent_id pointing at it, AND a SCHOOL_ADMIN user (gschiemann@e-arc.com). So a real parent-tenant admin is locked out of the parent feature. Either SCHOOL_ADMIN of a parent should see the roll-up, or the data model should forbid SCHOOL_ADMIN on a parent tenant.

findings.title: Flagship 50-location demo renders as 0/150 online (sea of red) — all child screens have NULL last_ping_at
findings.userRepro: Log in as corporate@acme-coffee.demo (DISTRICT_ADMIN, Acme Coffee Corporate) and view the dashboard. The 'Corporate — fleet overview' header will show 'Online 0 / 150 offline' and every one of the 50 locations renders with a red 'down' dot, because the live-status recompute correctly flips every never-pinged screen to OFFLINE. The demo that's meant to showcase fleet health looks like a total outage.
findings.evidence: DB: simulating the /screens/fleet aggregation for Acme Corporate returns fleet_total=150, never_pinged=150, live_online=0 (all 150 child screens have last_ping_at IS NULL). The status recompute (screens.controller.ts:1096-1103: isAlive = last && (now-last) < 35s → else OFFLINE) is CORRECT — the bug is seed data: the 150-screen demo (task #235) created screens but never simulated heartbeats, unlike the Dodgers screens which have fresh pings. Fix is data-side (seed periodic last_ping_at for demo child screens), but it makes a working feature look broken to anyone demoing the multi-location story.

findings.title: Per-tenant 'Sites' KPI + Sites roll-up table show all screens as 'Unassigned' for leaf locations with no screen groups
findings.userRepro: Switch into any Acme leaf location (e.g. acme-dallas) or Springfield Elementary. The 'Sites' KPI counts screen groups; the 'Sites — Health by location' table groups screens by screenGroupId. With no groups created, all 3 screens land in a single 'Unassigned' row and the Sites KPI reads 0 sites even though the location has screens.
findings.evidence: DB: every Acme leaf has grouped=0, unassigned=3 (no screen_groups rows). The sites useMemo (dashboard/page.tsx:159-188) buckets ungrouped screens into a single `_unassigned` row, and the 'Sites' KPI (L607-614) uses `sites.length` which would be 1 ('Unassigned') — technically not zero, but the card sub-label 'Health by location' implies physical sites, not group membership. For a coffee shop with 3 screens and no concept of 'groups', the Sites card is confusing noise. Consider hiding the Sites card/roll-up entirely when zero groups exist.

findings.title: Dead hook useDashboardStats / unused GET /stats/overview — dashboard computes all stats client-side
findings.userRepro: Not user-visible. The dashboard never calls useDashboardStats; it derives every KPI from the already-fetched list queries. The /stats/overview endpoint exists and is auth-gated (401) but has no frontend consumer.
findings.evidence: grep for useDashboardStats across apps/web/src returns zero callers outside its own definition file. The dashboard's KPIs all come from client-side useMemo over useScreens/usePlaylists/useAssets/useSchedules. Backend GET /stats/overview (stats.controller.ts:13) returns 401 unauthed and is functional but orphaned. Minor: dead code / a second source of truth for the same numbers that could drift if ever wired up. Cleanup, not a bug.

audits.summary:
The screens / pairing / manifest surface is REAL and works end-to-end — verified live, not a costume. I hit the production API unauthenticated: POST /screens/register created a Screen row, returned pairing code PHY7PS + a real device JWT (kind:'device', sub=screenId, 15-min exp); that JWT then fetched its own manifest (200, with a clear emptyReason:NO_SCHEDULE + human-readable message), and a cross-screen manifest fetch with the same token correctly 403'd ("Device token does not match screen") — tenant/device isolation holds. DB confirms genuine usage: 185 screens, 163 bound to tenants, 22 unpaired-with-code (pairing flow in active use), 4 online in the last 5 min. The live water-polo LED ("LED Score Board", Dodgers tenant) carries canvas_w=960/canvas_h=1080, orientation=AUTO, hardware_model=novastar-taurus, with an active board game — the real install. The manifest endpoint correctly carries orientation, canvasW/H, repeats, gpio, emergency state, and tenant-scoped schedules in the NORMAL and SCOREBOARD branches. The pair modal (uppercase-normalize, QR option, error surfacing, refetch) is clean.

The notable defect: the EMERGENCY-branch manifest payload (screens.controller.ts:2851-2890) omits canvasW/canvasH/repeats — the exact fields the 2026-06-24 commit (#9b47556) added to the SCOREBOARD branch (lines 2921-2923) and that the NORMAL branch carries (lines 3160-3168) "without these the player renders at device resolution → cut off on a narrow LED poster (960×1080)." So during an emergency on the live 960×1080 LED, the alert content can render at 1920 device-res and be cut off — on the most safety-critical content path, on the one real LED in production. The player retains the prior canvas from localStorage, which masks it in the steady state, but a boot-into-emergency or post-cache-wipe loses it. Plus the emergency branch keys isPortrait off Screen.resolution ("1920×1080"=landscape) not the actual canvas (960 wide) — so it also picks the wrong landscape emergency template for the narrow LED. Secondary: the canvas-set UI only offers 320×N widths at a fixed 1080 height (6 presets), so true ribbons (e.g. 1920×360) or non-panel LEDs can't be configured; 23 orphan unpaired Screen rows accumulate with no janitor cron; emergency-state cache invalidation is in-process only (bounded 2s on multi-replica).

findings.title: Emergency manifest branch drops LED canvasW/canvasH/repeats — alert content cut off on the live 960×1080 water-polo LED
findings.userRepro: On the Dodgers 'LED Score Board' (canvas_w=960, canvas_h=1080, novastar-taurus — the real water-polo install), trigger any tenant or per-screen emergency. The emergency-branch manifest payload returns only {orientation, playlists, ...} with NO canvasW/canvasH/repeats, so the player's TemplateScaler renders the emergency content at the controller's native 1920-wide viewport instead of the 960-wide LED. The alert is squeezed/cut off on the narrow poster. (In steady state the player retains the prior 960 canvas from localStorage/CSS, masking it; a boot-into-emergency, OTA reinstall, or cache wipe surfaces it.) Compare: the SCOREBOARD branch at 2921-2923 and NORMAL branch at 3160-3168 both DO send these fields.
findings.evidence: Code: emergency branch return (2851-2890) emits `orientation: isPortrait?'portrait':'landscape'` + `playlists` but no canvasW/canvasH/repeats; the scoreboard branch comment (2915-2920) literally says 'Without these the player renders the board at the device resolution (1920) → cut off on a narrow LED poster (960×1080)' — the same risk, unfixed for the emergency path. Player consumes manifest.canvasW only inside `if (cw && ch)` (apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:2910-2959), so absent fields = no re-apply. DB: the live LED Score Board row has canvas_w=960, canvas_h=1080, hardware_model='novastar-taurus', board_game_active=true.

findings.title: Emergency branch computes portrait/landscape from Screen.resolution, not the LED canvas — wrong-orientation emergency template on narrow LEDs
findings.userRepro: Same LED Score Board: resolution is stored '1920×1080' (landscape) but the physical LED canvas is 960×1080 (narrow/portrait-shaped). During an emergency the isPortrait check parses Screen.resolution ('1920×1080' → landscape) and serves the LANDSCAPE emergency playlist/fallback template (1920×1080), and the BULLETPROOF fallback sizes the text zone at canvasW=1920/canvasH=1080. On a 960-wide LED that text is built for the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: isPortrait regex at 2624-2629 reads only `screen.resolution`; the fallback template at 2807-2848 sets canvasW/canvasH from isPortrait (1920×1080 landscape) ignoring the screen's actual canvas_w/canvas_h (960×1080). The 960×1080 canvas — which IS stored on the row — is never consulted in the emergency branch. Live DB proof: resolution='1920×1080' AND canvas_w=960 on the same screen (id 7b072185-3399-433e-8151-12fe70c6dcdd).

findings.title: LED canvas picker is hardcoded to 320×N width at fixed 1080 height — no ribbon / non-panel / arbitrary canvas configurable from the dashboard
findings.userRepro: Open a screen's settings drawer → 'LED canvas (320×1080 panels)'. The only options are Off + buttons 1-6, each setting canvasW=320×N, canvasH=1080. An operator with a true ribbon LED (e.g. 1920×360) or any non-(320·N)×1080 LED cannot set its canvas at all. The label also calls a single 960×1080 LED '3 panels', which is misleading for a non-segmented poster.
findings.evidence: Buttons map `[1..6].map(n => ({w: 320*n, h: 1080}))` (482-484); panel-count inference assumes canvasH===1080 && canvasW%320===0 (page.tsx:378). The API PUT /screens/:id/canvas accepts any 32-8192 integer (screens.controller.ts:1585-1626), so the limitation is purely the UI — the backend already supports free-form canvas, but the operator has no way to enter it.

findings.title: Orphan unpaired Screen rows accumulate forever — no janitor/cron prunes them
findings.userRepro: Any kiosk (or anyone) that POSTs /screens/register but never gets claimed leaves a PENDING, tenant_id=NULL Screen row with a live pairing code. There is no admin-visible cleanup and no scheduled prune; rows pile up indefinitely.
findings.evidence: DB: 23 PENDING/unbound Screen rows, 22 older than 14 days. The register handler comment (197-204) acknowledges 'an unauthenticated attacker spamming fingerprints can only create orphan Screen rows that admins never claim — cleanup script is a separate problem.' No such cleanup exists in the screens module (only screen-wedge-detector.cron.ts, which targets online wedged screens, not orphans). Low risk (no data leak), but unbounded growth + the public unthrottled register endpoint (per-IP throttle removed, v5) means a single client can balloon the table.

findings.title: Emergency-state cache invalidation is in-process only — other API replicas serve stale tenant emergency state for up to 2s
findings.userRepro: On a multi-replica deploy, trigger an emergency. The replica that handled POST /emergency/trigger clears its in-memory tenant-state cache (emergency.controller.ts:575); other replicas keep returning the prior INACTIVE state from getTenantState() until the 2s TTL expires. A kiosk polling a stale replica could see the alert up to ~2s late on the manifest path.
findings.evidence: invalidateTenantState (manifest-hot-cache.ts:71) mutates a module-local Map — not Redis. TENANT_STATE_TTL_MS=2_000 (line 34). The WS/SSE fan-out path is the primary (fast) channel; the manifest poll is the documented backstop, so impact is bounded to ~2s on the slow path and only matters if Railway runs >1 API replica. Note as a known-bounded gap, not a hard failure.

costumes: Cross-location playlist publishing: writes Asset.status='APPROVED' which NO playback path accepts (manifest + /playback require 'PUBLISHED'), so HQ-pushed content silently never renders on child screens
AssetPicker file chooser advertises image/svg+xml and image/avif in its accept attribute, but the server ALLOWED_TYPES rejects both — selecting one fails after the operator picks it

findings.title: Cross-location published assets get status 'APPROVED' but every playback path only serves 'PUBLISHED' — corporate-pushed content silently never reaches child screens
findings.userRepro: As HQ/district admin, use fleet-wide 'cross-location playlist publishing' (shipped, task #233) to push a playlist with media to child locations. The child operator sees the playlist + assets scheduled, but the assets never display on any child screen — the manifest filters them out. No error is shown anywhere.
findings.evidence: ensureChildAsset() at line 166 sets status:'APPROVED' with comment 'corporate-pushed content is pre-approved'. The player manifest builders (screens.controller.ts:2732 and :2987) filter `where: { asset: { status: 'PUBLISHED' } }`, and the single-asset /:id/playback endpoint (assets.controller.ts:1337) requires status:'PUBLISHED'. 'APPROVED' is not a value the approve() endpoint or initialAssetStatus() ever produces (those use PUBLISHED/PENDING_APPROVAL/ARCHIVED). DB PROOF: 5 live assets exist with status='APPROVED' (2 real PDFs incl. ARC_XBoard brochure, 3 corp-memo.png), and ALL 5 are referenced by playlist_items (in_playlist_items >= 1) — i.e. operators have already scheduled content that can never play. Fix: write 'PUBLISHED' (or backfill the 5 rows + map APPROVED->PUBLISHED in the manifest where-clause).

findings.title: AssetPicker advertises SVG + AVIF uploads the server rejects (accept-list mismatch → dead-end after file selection)
findings.file: apps/web/src/components/assets/AssetPicker.tsx:85-90 (accept includes image/svg+xml, image/avif) vs apps/api/src/assets/assets.controller.ts:44-49 (ALLOWED_TYPES excludes both; SVG intentionally disabled lines 39-43, AVIF never added)
findings.userRepro: Open any image picker (e.g. in template builder → choose image → 'Upload'), the native file chooser shows SVG and AVIF as selectable. Pick a .svg or .avif and it uploads-then-fails: /assets/presign returns 415 'File type is not supported' AFTER the operator already chose the file.

Server normalizeMimeType/assertUploadIntent only allows the ALLOWED_TYPES list (no svg, no avif). The main assets page ACCEPT_STRING (page.tsx:31) correctly omits both — only the picker is out of sync. Result is a confusing post-select failure rather than the file being greyed-out. Note: this is a UX dead-end, not data loss; uploads of supported types work fine.

findings.title: 16 duplicate-content assets stored (storage waste) — dedup exists for cross-location children but not for an operator re-uploading the same file
findings.file: apps/api/src/assets/assets.controller.ts:617-826 (completeUpload always creates a new Asset + new storage object); dedup only in playlist-distribution.service.ts:155-159
findings.userRepro: Upload the same image/video twice (e.g. corp-memo.png was uploaded 3x at 12:20/12:27/12:27 on 2026-06-03). Each creates a separate storage object + Asset row.
findings.evidence: DB: 97 assets carry a file_hash but only 81 distinct hashes => 16 byte-identical duplicates stored and paid for. The upload path computes fileHash (assets.controller.ts:947) but never checks for an existing same-hash asset before creating. ensureChildAsset (distribution) DOES dedup on fileHash — the everyday upload path does not. Low severity: correctness is fine, it's storage/egress waste + library clutter.

audits.summary: Assets/upload is a genuinely solid, well-engineered surface — NOT a costume overall. I verified the full chain works end-to-end live: presign -> direct Supabase signed PUT -> complete-upload with server-side sharp optimization (image/png path shows processing_meta on 16 rows, jpeg->webp re-encode confirmed), SHA-256 hashing, role-gated approval (admins auto-PUBLISH, contributors -> PENDING_APPROVAL, manifest strictly filters to PUBLISHED at screens.controller.ts:2732/2987), folder CRUD with tenant isolation, and previews (image transform thumbs, video, lazy-PDF iframe). Auth gating is real (GET /assets => 401, POST => 403 CSRF). The much-feared Supabase EGRESS regression is NOT a finding: I probed live objects and once Cloudflare warms, full GETs serve `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` with `cf-cache-status: HIT` on both a new optimized webp AND a legacy 2026-05-26 PDF (the backfill ran). The first cold/HEAD probe showed no-cache, exactly as the code comment warns, so I re-probed rather than asserting. THE REAL BUG (P0): cross-location playlist publishing (playlist-distribution.service.ts:166) stamps copied assets with status='APPROVED', but every playback path only accepts 'PUBLISHED' — 5 live APPROVED assets, all already in playlists, can never render on a child screen, with zero error surfaced. That's a shipped feature (task #233) writing dead content. Two P2s: AssetPicker offers SVG/AVIF the server rejects (post-select dead-end), and 16 byte-identical duplicate files are stored because the everyday upload path skips the hash-dedup that the distribution path uses. Design A (Media Library is clean, well-laid-out, $$$ -tier), UX B+ (clear 30s upload happy path; the SVG/AVIF and silent-non-render issues dock it), Functionality B (works for direct uploads; the cross-location distribution path is broken).

costumes: "Schedule a window" publish option (Step 4): a real-looking radio card that creates the schedule as is_active=false, so the playlist is silently never served to any screen — looks done, does nothing

findings.title: "Schedule a window" creates the schedule INACTIVE — playlist silently never plays
findings.userRepro: New Playlist → name it, pick media → pick a screen → Step 4 choose "Schedule a window" (e.g. Mon–Fri 08:00–15:00) → Create Playlist. The wizard succeeds and hands you to the editor, but the schedule is written with is_active=false. The manifest resolver only serves is_active=true schedules, so the screen NEVER plays the playlist — even inside the window — and the operator gets no error. (They'd have to notice the card shows "○ Off" and manually toggle it on.)
findings.evidence: handleCreate builds schedules with `isActive: activateImmediately` (line 860). When the operator picks "Schedule a window", activateImmediately=false, so isActive=false. Backend confirms: schedules.controller.ts:101 `willBeActive = !isContributor && body.isActive !== false` → false → row saved inactive. Manifest only serves active: screens.controller.ts:2972 `{ isActive: true }`. DB proof: the ONLY scheduled-window playlist ever made via the wizard ("Test mobile", 2026-05-31) is is_active=false with a valid window (Mon-Fri 08:00-15:00, mode=replace) — it has never played. Aggregate: of 40 schedules, 28 are inactive. The "Activate immediately" path works correctly (isActive=true); only the scheduled-window path is broken. Bug present since the wizard's first commit 8fb66551, never fixed (git log -S). Deployed commit 79720947 is newer than local HEAD fdcae7fa so confirm against prod, but the line is the original implementation with no fix in any local commit.

findings.title: Picking a screen group creates per-screen schedules, not a group schedule — group membership changes won't auto-apply
findings.userRepro: In Step 3 click a screen group (one-click "adds all its screens"). The wizard expands the group to individual screen IDs and creates one schedule PER screen. If you later add a 4th screen to that group, the new screen does NOT get the playlist — unlike a true group-scoped schedule.
findings.evidence: onPickGroup pushes member screen IDs into selectedScreenIds; handleCreate maps every selectedScreenId to a `{ screenId }` schedule and never sends `screenGroupId`. DB confirms: of 40 schedules, screen_group_id IS NOT NULL on 0 rows, screen_id on all 40 — the system supports group-scoped schedules (schedules.controller.ts:87-94 validates screenGroupId) but the wizard never creates one. Functional for the moment-of-creation fleet; brittle for dynamic groups.

findings.title: Step 5 Review lets you reach Create with "No days picked" — a window schedule that runs zero days
findings.userRepro: Step 4 "Schedule a window" → deselect every weekday → Next. Step 5 shows the schedule as "No days picked · 08:00–15:00" but Create Playlist is still enabled. You create a schedule whose daysOfWeek is empty.
findings.evidence: Step5Review computes `parts.push('No days picked')` when schedDays.length===0 but there is no validation gate blocking Create; nextDisabled only checks steps 1 and 2 (lines 968-970). The schedule schema accepts an empty/absent daysOfWeek. Combined with the P0 (inactive anyway), a window with no days is a second silent dead-end. Low frequency but it's a footgun with no warning.

audits.summary: The PlaylistCreateWizard is a genuinely strong, real feature — not a costume overall. It writes real rows end-to-end: the most recent playlist (\"Brooky\", created the day of this audit) has 5 items + 1 active schedule, durations are sane, and the dnd reorder / per-item duration / auto-video-length / folder browsing / group expansion all work. Backend is well-guarded (tenant-scoped template + asset ownership checks, Zod validation, transactional item replace). DESIGN is A (clean 5-step modal, step indicator, polished review). UX is B (clear flow, but the broken path gives zero feedback). FUNCTIONALITY is C because of ONE P0: the \"Activate immediately\" path works, but the \"Schedule a window\" path writes the schedule as is_active=false (PlaylistCreateWizard.tsx:860 `isActive: activateImmediately`), and the manifest only serves active schedules (screens.controller.ts:2972) — so a scheduled-window playlist silently never reaches any screen and the operator is told it succeeded. This is proven against live DB: the one scheduled-window playlist ever created via the wizard is inactive and has never played. The \"Schedule a window\" card is effectively a costume — looks done, does nothing. Fix: send isActive=true for non-CONTRIBUTOR scheduled-window creations (the days/time window already gates WHEN it plays; isActive should reflect whether the schedule is enabled, which it should be). Two P2s: group picks degrade to per-screen schedules (no dynamic group membership), and Review lets you Create a \"No days picked\" window with no warning. Staleness note: local HEAD (fdcae7fa) is behind deployed (79720947); the P0 line is the wizard's original unmodified implementation, so it is almost certainly live, but worth a prod re-confirm.

The templates gallery is genuinely strong: 397 templates in prod (373 system / 24 custom), including 145 EXTERNAL_HTML boards each pointing at a real served HTML file (all probed at HTTP 200), plus 50 holiday boards. The EXTERNAL_HTML render path (sandboxed null-origin iframe, base64url override passthrough, freeze-for-thumbnail, click-to-edit "hot zones") is well-engineered and the shim sweep is clean — every hs/signage/fitness board carries educms-field-click. Auth is correctly enforced (GET /templates -> 401, POST /imports/design -> 403 unauthed).

Import 2.0 is NOT a costume — I traced and verified the real machinery. The PPTX parser uses JSZip + fast-xml-parser, reads <a:off>/<a:ext> EMU rectangles, walks <p:sp> text shapes and <p:pic> pictures into positioned TEXT/IMAGE template_zones, uploads embedded media as Assets, and has 12 passing unit tests. The PDF parser uses pdfjs-dist (installed + bundled, dep in apps/api/package.json) legacy build, page.getTextContent() → positioned editable TEXT zones. Both have a graceful try/catch fallback to a single-image template. Deployed prod (SHA 79720947) matches local code on this surface.

HOWEVER two real problems: (1) ZERO production usage — IMPORT_DESIGN has 0 rows out of 5505 audit_logs, and not a single custom template in prod came from an import (all 24 are AI-generated welcome/menu scenes or test rows). The feature has never been exercised by a real operator. (2) The structured PDF path throws away ALL visual fidelity: the controller deliberately passes resolveMedia: () => null and never sets pageBackgroundUrl, so a PDF imported "as a Template" becomes floating editable text on a blank white canvas — no background, no logos, no colors, no vector art. Since real-world design PDFs (Canva exports, flyers) are overwhelmingly image/vector, the operator's "fully editable template" promise produces a near-blank or text-only result that looks nothing like their source. This is the gap between the marketing copy ("text and images come through as editable layers, not a flat picture") and reality for PDF.

Verdict: gallery is A-/board-worthy; import works end-to-end mechanically but the PDF result will disappoint and the whole feature is unproven in production.

findings.title: Structured PDF import discards ALL visual fidelity (no background, no images, no colors) — produces text-on-blank-white that looks nothing like the source
findings.file: apps/api/src/imports/imports.controller.ts:365-381 (built = buildTemplates(doc, { resolveMedia: () => null }); no pageBackgroundUrl); apps/api/src/imports/parsers/pdf-parser.ts:248 (returns { pages, media: [] })
findings.userRepro: On /[schoolId]/templates/imports, drop a normal design PDF (e.g. a Canva/flyer export with a photo, logo and colored background). Click 'Add to Templates'. Open the resulting template in the builder. You get the page's text laid out in roughly the right positions on a plain #ffffff canvas — the background photo, logo, brand colors and any vector art are gone. The auto-created Playlist keeps the real PDF for pixel-faithful PLAYBACK, but the 'Template' the operator was steered toward (primary brand-colored button) is the disappointing one.

findings.title: Import preview step can't actually show what the editable template will look like — operator commits blind
findings.file: apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/templates/imports/page.tsx:417-463 (FilePreview shows the raw source file, not the parsed result)
findings.userRepro: On /templates/imports, drop a PPTX. The 'Preview' step shows a generic 'PowerPoint ready to import' card (no slide thumbnails). Drop a PDF: it shows the native browser PDF viewer of the ORIGINAL file. Either way you click 'Add to Templates' without ever seeing the parsed/editable output, then discover (especially for PDF, see P1) it looks different from the source.

The widgets panel is correctly VariantPicker (BuilderShell.tsx:697), not the dead WidgetPalette. audits.summary: The KNOWN BUG is confirmed in production data, and I traced its exact cause. Backend schedule RESOLUTION is correct: the manifest query (screens.controller.ts:2961-2974) resolves both per-screen `{screenId}` and per-group `{screenGroupId}` schedules, so a single group schedule WOULD reach every screen in the group. The defect is on the WRITE/UI side. The primary creation flow — the New Playlist wizard (the file header literally calls it "operator's primary creation flow") — can NEVER create a group schedule: its group picker (playlists/page.tsx:1066-1080 `onPickGroup`) explodes a group into individual screen IDs, and handleCreate (PlaylistCreateWizard.tsx:850-861) only ever emits `{screenId}` rows. DB proof: the Dodgers tenant has 30 schedules and EVERY single one has screen_group_id = NULL — not one group schedule exists, despite a "Work" group with 4 screens (G43, M43, TC22, LED Score Board). The lived symptom is worse than "1 of 3": those 4 group screens are currently on THREE different playlists (G43/M43=Brookfield Images, TC22=Brookfield, LED=Brooky) because per-screen replace-mode publishing only displaces schedules on the one target it writes, so screens silently drift apart. The standalone Publish modal (playlists/page.tsx:2306-2323) DOES support "Entire Group" correctly (emits one group- target, disables member checkboxes) — so the platform is capable of group publishing; the wizard just doesn't use it, and PlaylistDistributionService.scheduleLive (fleet publish, playlist-distribution.service.ts:232-252) is also per-screen-only. Secondary: when a screen matches both a per-screen and a group active schedule, the manifest returns BOTH playlists with no priority/dedup (screens.controller.ts:3007-3034). findings.title: Primary publish flow (New Playlist wizard) cannot create a group schedule — explodes groups to per-screen, so members silently drift onto different playlists

findings.title: Per-replica in-memory board cache: invalidate-on-write only clears the local replica
findings.userRepro: On a multi-replica deploy, a score change handled by replica A may not invalidate replica B's cache, so a board polling replica B can show up-to-1s-stale data right after a score.
findings.evidence: boardCache is an instance Map, invalidateBoardCache only deletes from the local replica. Mitigated by the 1s TTL (bounds staleness to one poll window of 750ms) so impact is minor, but the explicit invalidation is a no-op across replicas — only the TTL actually bounds cross-replica staleness.

The server clears via signMessage('ALL_CLEAR', ...) (3 callsites) but the player only clears a pushed message on type ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE — a type the server emits NOWHERE. This is exactly the "stuck on lockdown after all-clear" class the OVERRIDE path was hardened against, re-introduced on the message path.

Secondary: the broadcast SUCCESS path has no E2E test (only the failure path is covered, per task #206), consistent with this gap going unnoticed.

findings.title: WS-delivered SOS / TEXT_BROADCAST / MEDIA_ALERT overlay cannot be cleared by operator all-clear — server sends 'ALL_CLEAR', player only clears on 'ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE' (never emitted)
findings.userRepro: Operator fires a Staff SOS (or Text Broadcast / Media Alert) from the dashboard while the kiosk's WebSocket is healthy — the overlay shows on the wall. Operator then hits all-clear for that message. The overlay STAYS on screen; it does not dismiss. It only disappears when the message's own expiry elapses (5 min for broadcast, 30 min SOS, 60 min media alert). The operator's clear action is a visible no-op on the affected screen.
findings.evidence: Server clears via this.signer.signMessage('ALL_CLEAR', ...) at emergency.controller.ts:664 (clearEmergency) and :1149 (clearMessage), and screen-emergency.controller.ts:467. grep proves ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE is emitted NOWHERE in apps/api or packages/ws-events. The player's ALL_CLEAR handler (player/page.tsx:3684 & 3938) only calls fetchContent(); the only code that calls setPushedEmergencyMessage(null) is gated on type==='ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE' (lines 3741, 3971). fetchContent() reconciles `activeEmergency` from the manifest but never touches `pushedEmergencyMessage`. Confirmed live: the production bundle at https://venue-os.app/_next/static/chunks/0qgntqxrah.jo.js contains both 'ALL_CLEAR' (2x) and 'ALL_CLEAR_MESSAGE' (3x), so the deployed player has the broken contract.

findings.title: No backstop can reconcile a stuck pushed-message overlay: self-poll is disabled while a WS message is present, and the manifest emergency field doesn't carry SOS/broadcast/media types
findings.userRepro: Same as above. Even though the system advertises an HTTP-poll backstop for life-safety messages, that backstop cannot rescue an already-displayed WS message after all-clear — so the stuck overlay persists until expiry with no recovery path other than rebooting the kiosk or re-pairing.
findings.evidence: EmergencyOverlay.tsx:81 `if (message || !apiUrl) return;` — the self-poll useEffect short-circuits whenever a WS-pushed `message` prop is set, so it never re-queries /emergency/messages to notice the message is now clearedAt. Separately, the manifest emergency block (screens.controller.ts ~2600-2660) surfaces only Tenant.emergencyStatus + per-screen ScreenEmergencyOverride (OVERRIDE-class) — grep shows NO sos/broadcast/media/emergencyMessage references in that block — so the 10s manifest poll the player uses to self-correct OVERRIDE state has no visibility into pushed messages.

audits.summary:
Billing is architecturally strong but FUNCTIONALLY BROKEN end-to-end on the live prod deploy, and it is dressed as "live" when it is a Stripe TEST sandbox. The code path is real and well-built: BillingController (checkout/portal/invoices/status), an unauthenticated signature-verified webhook, idempotency via processed_stripe_events, out-of-order protection via stripeLastEventCreatedAt, AuditLog on every License mutation, a SERIALIZABLE+withDbRetry seat-pair tx, and a daily License↔Stripe reconcile cron. None of it is a stub.

BUT three things make it not work for a real customer right now:

1) P0 COSTUME — prod is wired to STRIPE TEST KEYS. Railway prod env has STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_..., plus test price IDs and a whsec. So StripeService.enabled() returns true and GET /billing/status truthfully says "Stripe is configured — checkout, portal and invoices are live," while in reality a customer who clicks "Choose Monthly" is sent to Stripe TEST-mode Checkout (test cards only, no real money is ever collected). This is the exact "live-looking but not real" pattern. DB proof: 65 tenants, only 1 License row (a PILOT/COMP), 0 stripe subscriptions, 0 stripe customers, 0 card-billed licenses — billing has literally never collected a dollar in prod.

2) P0 — the webhook cannot receive ANY Stripe event. main.ts boots with NestFactory rawBody:true (which the webhook depends on for signature verification) but then registers a SECOND, global express.json()/urlencoded() body parser at lines 80-81. The global express parser consumes the request stream before Nest's raw-body capture, so req.rawBody is undefined on the webhook route. LIVE PROOF: POSTing the webhook WITH a valid string stripe-signature header still returns "Missing raw body or stripe-signature header" (HTTP 400) — that branch only fires when req.rawBody is falsy. DB PROOF: processed_stripe_events is empty and there are 0 STRIPE_WEBHOOK_* audit rows despite 5,534 audit rows total (the audit pipeline is healthy, just no Stripe events ever arrive). Consequence: even if real keys were swapped in, checkout.session.completed / subscription.* / invoice.payment_failed would all 400 → the License row never syncs → a paying customer's plan never activates, past-due is never recorded, cancellation never propagates. The only safety net (the reconcile cron) also no-ops because no License ever gets a stripeSubscriptionId. The bug is invisible to tests because the only Stripe test (stripe.service.spec.ts) is a unit test that passes a Buffer directly and never exercises the HTTP body-parser stack — there is no webhook integration test.

3) P1 — "Free trial" tier is misleading copy with no behavior. The plans grid renders a FREE_TRIAL card saying "14 days / up to 3 screens" but it shows an inert "Default — no card needed" label (no button), and POST /billing/activate-trial is explicitly read-only (returns committed:false, persists nothing). There is no 14-day clock and no 3-screen cap anywhere — the real default (no License row) is a perpetual PILOT with seatLimit=1000 (LicenseService.PILOT_SEAT_LIMIT). So the marquee "14-day trial" the page advertises does not exist as a real lifecycle.

Net: a superintendent would see a polished billing page (design A-) and could navigate it (ux B), but no real money can be collected and no subscription can ever activate (func D). Stale-vs-prod note: findings 1 and 2 are confirmed against the LIVE prod Railway env + live API probes + live DB, not just the local tree.

findings.title: Webhook can't receive ANY Stripe event — global express.json() shadows Nest rawBody (subscriptions never activate)
findings.userRepro: Configure real Stripe, register the webhook at POST /api/v1/billing/webhook, complete a Checkout. Stripe sends checkout.session.completed; the endpoint returns HTTP 400 'Missing raw body or stripe-signature header' and the customer's License/plan never updates. Reproduce the root cause live: curl -X POST -H 'stripe-signature: t=1,v1=deadbeef' --data-binary '{...}' https://api-production-39a1.up.railway.app/api/v1/billing/webhook → returns 'Missing raw body or stripe-signature header' even though the signature header IS present, proving req.rawBody is undefined.
findings.evidence: main.ts:42 creates the app with { rawBody: true } (Nest's internal raw-body capture), but lines 80-81 then register a SECOND global body parser: app.use(expressBody.json({limit:'5mb'})) and urlencoded(). The global express parser drains the request stream before Nest's raw-body capture runs, leaving req.rawBody undefined. The webhook guard at billing-webhook.controller.ts:37 (`if (!rawBody || typeof signature !== 'string')`) therefore always trips. Live probe: webhook with a valid string signature header still returns the !rawBody branch message (not the downstream 'Stripe webhook verification failed' message that constructWebhookEvent would throw). DB confirms the effect: processed_stripe_events = 0 rows and audit_logs WHERE action LIKE 'STRIPE_WEBHOOK%' = 0, while audit_logs total = 5534 (pipeline healthy). The only Stripe test (stripe.service.spec.ts) is a unit test that injects a Buffer directly and never hits the HTTP body parser, so CI is green while the integration is dead. NOTE: pos/pos-oauth.controller.ts:289 reads req.rawBody the same way and is likely equally affected.

findings.title: Prod billing is wired to Stripe TEST keys — status/page claim 'live' but no real money can be collected (costume)
findings.userRepro: On prod, an admin opens Settings → Billing, sees real plans and a working 'Choose Monthly/Annual' button, clicks it, and is redirected to a Stripe-hosted Checkout that ONLY accepts test cards (4242 4242 4242 4242). A real customer card is declined / nothing is actually charged. GET /billing/status reports 'Stripe is configured — checkout, portal and invoices are live.'
findings.evidence: Railway production variables (RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_NAME=production) show STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_51TYfFD..., STRIPE_PRICE_MONTHLY/ANNUAL=price_... and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... all set. StripeService.enabled() (stripe.service.ts:111) returns !!process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = true, so checkoutForTenant builds a REAL (test-mode) Stripe Checkout session (stripe.service.ts:233-245) and billing.controller status (line 123-125) asserts billing is live. DB reality: licenses table has 1 row (tier=PILOT, billing_mode=COMP); with_stripe_sub=0, with_stripe_cust=0, card_billed=0 across 65 tenants — zero real revenue has ever flowed. This is 'live-looking but a sandbox.' (Memory: 'Stripe TEST→live' is a known unshipped launch blocker — confirmed still test on prod.)

findings.title: 'Free trial' tier is advertised (14 days / 3 screens) but is inert — no button, no trial clock, no 3-seat cap
findings.userRepro: On Settings → Billing, the Plans grid shows a 'Free trial — 14 days, up to 3 screens, no credit card needed' card. It has no actionable button (renders 'Default — no card needed') and there is no 14-day countdown or 3-screen enforcement anywhere in the app.
findings.evidence: TierTile (page.tsx:516-581): FREE_TRIAL has isPaid=false and isCurrent is only true if currentTier==='FREE_TRIAL' (never — the real default tier is PILOT), so it always renders the inert 'Default — no card needed' div (line 578-580) with the '14 days' cadence (line 521-522). POST /billing/activate-trial (billing.controller.ts:142-161) is explicitly read-only: returns committed:false and persists nothing. The actual default for a tenant with no License row (license.service.ts:49-57) is tier PILOT, status ACTIVE, expiresAt null (perpetual), seatLimit = PILOT_SEAT_LIMIT = 1000 (line 33). So the marketed 14-day/3-screen trial does not exist as a real lifecycle — misleading to a buyer.

findings.title: License-vs-tenant gap: 64 of 65 tenants have no License row → all default to a perpetual 1000-seat PILOT (no metering, no billing readiness)
findings.userRepro: As any tenant admin, open Settings → Billing: status shows ACTIVE / free pilot / up to ~1000 screens regardless of who you are; you can pair far more screens than any real plan allows, and there is no path that converts the tenant to a billable License without the (dead) webhook.
findings.evidence: DB: total_tenants=65 but total_licenses=1. getEffective() (license.service.ts:49-57) returns PILOT/ACTIVE/seatLimit=1000/expiresAt=null for every tenant lacking a License row, by design (PILOT_SEAT_LIMIT raised from 3→1000 on 2026-05-04 for internal testing, with an in-code TODO to drop it back before the first paying customer). Combined with findings P0-1/P0-2, the only way a tenant ever gets a real (CARD) License is the webhook upsert in syncLicenseFromSubscription (stripe.service.ts:496-523) — which can never fire because req.rawBody is undefined. So billing readiness is blocked on both ends.

findings.title: No webhook integration test — the body-parser regression (P0-1) is invisible to CI
findings.userRepro: N/A (developer-facing). Run pnpm --filter api test — Stripe coverage passes while the live webhook is non-functional.
findings.evidence: The single Stripe test file is stripe.service.spec.ts, a unit test that calls handleWebhookEvent with a fabricated event object / passes Buffers directly, bypassing the Express body-parser entirely. There is no e2e/integration test that POSTs a signed payload through main.ts's parser chain to assert req.rawBody is populated and the webhook returns 200. COSTUMES (look real, fail on this deploy): (1) SSO SAML — default-selected, fully-formed, savable & enable-able in the UI, but passport-saml is intentionally NOT installed (CVE avoidance) so every SAML login 503s; OIDC beside it IS real. Comms (Twilio/Slack/Sendgrid) have no operator settings UI (N/A; previously flipped COMING_SOON). Net: a non-IT operator on this prod deploy can fully use Users/AI-keys/Streaming/Audit, but will hit a dead end on POS, SAML-SSO, and Clever — hence worksForEndUser=false for the surface as a whole. Findings are NOT stale: live commit 79720947 is in local history and the integration code paths reviewed are unchanged vs. local HEAD. findings.title: React #418 hydration mismatch thrown on EVERY player page load (live prod)
findings.file: apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:1 ("use client", no `export const dynamic`/ssr:false); window-derived strings rendered at first paint (e.g. DISPLAY resolution, VP LED line)
findings.userRepro: Open https://venue-os.app/player in any browser, open devtools console. On load (and reloads) you get: 'Error: Minified React error #418' (Text content did not match server-rendered HTML). Reproduced 3x across 2 navigations in live Chrome.
findings.evidence: Live console on venue-os.app/player throws Minified React error #418 every load (captured 11:23:59, 11:24:31, 11:24:32). #418 = SSR/client text mismatch. Page is `use client` with no force-dynamic; the splash renders window-dependent text (the live splash shows 'DISPLAY 1710×1112' and 'VP 1200×842 LED' which are window.screen-derived — empty/different at SSR). React recovers via client re-render on modern V8, but per CLAUDE.md cross-browser rules (#1/#6) hydration mismatches are the exact class that breaks on WebKit/Chromium-83 (Taurus) where the player MUST run. The root <body> has suppressHydrationWarning but that only covers the body node, not the deep player tree. Fix: gate window-derived render behind a mounted flag (render placeholder on first paint) or `export const dynamic='force-dynamic'` + client-only guard.

findings.title: Liveness /health reports db:'degraded' against a fully-working DB due to an over-tight 400ms query budget
findings.userRepro: curl https://api-production-39a1.up.railway.app/api/v1/health → returns {"status":"degraded","db":"degraded","redis":"ok"} even though the DB is healthy and serving traffic.
findings.evidence: Live health shows db:degraded, yet the DB is fully reachable: my read-only postgres MCP returns 186 screens and 4 screens pinged within minutes (last_ping_at current, status updater live). The liveness probe gives `SELECT 1` only a 400ms budget vs the Supabase pgBouncer pooler from Railway, so a normal pooler round-trip intermittently exceeds it and is reported as degraded. Harmless to Railway (liveness always returns 200; readiness uses 1500ms) but it makes the ops dashboard / keep-warm pinger / frontend retry-banner cry wolf. Bump the liveness DB budget to ~800-1000ms (still well under Railway's healthcheck window).

audits.summary: Player + cross-cutting surface is in genuinely good shape and works end-to-end on real glass: 4 live screens (incl. a 2160×3840 portrait and the 'LED Score Board') pinged within minutes, the live pairing splash (venue-os.app/player) is polished and professional, and the heavy safeguards are REAL not costumes. No P0s found. The real issues: (P1) a React #418 hydration mismatch fires on EVERY live player load — currently self-recovers on modern Chrome but is exactly the cross-browser class CLAUDE.md warns breaks on WebKit/Taurus; (P1) KioskSplash still ships flex/grid `gap` to the Chromium-83 Taurus splash (the project's own task #129, still pending — splash spacing degrades, not a crash); plus three P2 polish/robustness items (backdrop-filter fallbacks in fitness/ms/animated widgets, the 'LandscapePortraitAuto' run-together orientation control, and an over-tight 400ms health-probe budget that falsely reports db:degraded). black.notable: A new human signing up on prod has a working experience: a polished two-column signup page (vertical picker, org name, auto slug, name, email, optional phone/address, password/confirm), all fields fill cleanly, and on submit the account is genuinely created and they are dropped onto the authed /onboarding/branding step (paste-your-URL auto-branding, with a Skip-for-now escape) — not stuck on /signup or /login. DB cross-check confirms it: tenant "Beta Test 1782411696398" (slug beta-test-1782411696398, vertical K12) and user beta+1782411696398@venue-os.app (role DISTRICT_ADMIN) were both created at 2026-06-26T01:21:44Z. The single most important problem is NOT in the product — it's in the persona-runner's verdict logic, which is misleading and would mask a real outage: its saved post-signup.json/dashboard.json both record finalUrl=/signup with the signup form still in the body, yet it reported all 12 steps "ok" (the screenshots 10/11/12 are identical frozen "Creating your workspace…" spinner frames). The runner captures page state during the async redirect and its success heuristic only fails if the URL contains /login, so a genuinely-stuck signup would still pass. A clean re-run I did with network capture proves the real behavior: POST /api/v1/signup returns 200 with a valid access_token JWT, the browser navigates to /onboarding/branding, and /branding/me then returns 200 once the token is stored. The 401s on /branding/me are a benign pre-auth race (branding fetched before the token lands; it self-heals on the next call) — worth eliminating so the console is clean and the runner stops conflating a redirect-in-flight snapshot with a failure. Bottom line: signup works end-to-end on prod; fix the persona-runner to assert on the post-redirect authed URL (and the signup POST 200 + access_token) rather than a snapshot taken mid-redirect.

Console noise (all the _rsc fetch "access control checks" errors) is benign WebKit RSC-prefetch behavior plus an expected pre-login 401 on /branding/me; netFailures empty, so nothing actually broke for the user.

A real human filling out the Firefox signup form has a broken experience: they complete every field (vertical, org name, workspace URL, name, email, phone, password + confirm), click "Create workspace," and then sit forever on a button stuck spinning "Creating your workspace…". The page NEVER advances — the final URL is still https://venue-os.app/signup and screenshots 10, 11, and 12 are identical (form + perpetual spinner). The damning part: the account WAS created server-side — public.tenants has "Beta Test 1782411795354" (slug beta-test-1782411795354, K12) and public.users has beta+1782411795354@venue-os.app as an ACTIVE DISTRICT_ADMIN, both stamped 01:23:25. So the backend succeeded but the browser never landed on an authed dashboard. The single most important problem: the post-signup client-side redirect/auth handoff fails in Firefox — one console "[api] Request failed (non-network)" plus aborted RSC prefetches to /login and /branding/me (NS_BINDING_ABORTED) — leaving the user stranded on a spinner with a silently-created account, no error, and no way forward. SECONDARY but serious: the persona-runner reports a FALSE GREEN (12/12 passed, including "authed-dashboard-renders"); its pass criteria don't check that the URL actually left /signup or that dashboard content rendered, so the harness would have told us signup works when it does not. synth.executiveSummary: The app is far more real than "costume" — signup, login, dashboard/fleet, screens/pairing, assets, the sports console, branding and the emergency core all work end-to-end on live prod. But money and AI are dark, several "shipped" features silently no-op, and security is propped on guessable secrets. Fix these first: (1) prod runs on guessable JWT/SESSION secrets — anyone who guesses them forges any session incl. SUPER_ADMIN; (2) Stripe webhook can't receive a single event (global express.json shadows rawBody) AND prod is on Stripe TEST keys — no money can ever be collected; (3) cross-location published assets get status APPROVED but playback only serves PUBLISHED — corporate-pushed content silently never displays; (4) the "Schedule a window"/group publish path writes inactive/per-screen schedules so playlists silently never play; (5) emergency SOS/broadcast overlays can't be cleared by all-clear. AI is 100% off (no platform key). Rate limiting is theater across signup/login/reset. Firefox signup strands users on a spinner. Tackle secrets + billing + the silent-no-op trio next.
